news.title: Visa Turns SMB Smartphones Into Payment Hubs, Targeting Emerging Market Share
news.body: Visa has launched Visa Pay, Visa Accept, and Visa Direct to enable small businesses in emerging markets to accept and manage payments directly via smartphones. This move positions Visa to capture share from local payment providers and accelerate the shift away from traditional POS hardware. Merchants gain lower-cost entry to digital payments, while regional acquirers face new competition on their home turf.

news.title: Mynt’s $1.5B GCash IPO Sets New Benchmark for Southeast Asian Fintech
news.body: Philippines-based Mynt is preparing a $1.5 billion IPO for its mobile wallet GCash, reported as the largest listing in the country’s history. The capital raise will fuel GCash’s expansion and intensify competition with regional fintechs and incumbent banks. Investors are likely to increase their focus on Southeast Asian digital finance, raising the bar for product innovation and customer acquisition.

news.title: JPMorgan Calls for Digital Assets to Meet Full Banking Rulebook
news.body: JPMorgan executives are urging regulators to apply existing banking rules to digital asset companies, arguing this would ensure consistent safeguards across the sector. If adopted, digital asset firms would face higher compliance costs and operational scrutiny, narrowing the regulatory gap with traditional banks. Institutional adoption of digital assets could accelerate as risk standards converge.

news.title: Ethereum’s 25% Price Drop Puts Spotlight on Stablecoin Infrastructure and Network Stability
news.body: Ethereum’s price fell 25% in June amid a major corporate restructuring, drawing attention to the institutional stablecoin economy built atop its network. The shakeup raises questions about Ethereum’s competitive position versus other blockchains for stablecoin issuance and settlement. Stablecoin issuers and institutional users may reassess their reliance on Ethereum if network stability concerns persist.

news.title: Stripe Expands Terminal to Japan, Targeting Omnichannel Commerce
news.body: Stripe has launched its Terminal product in Japan, enabling merchants to unify online and in-person payments through a single platform. This expansion allows Japanese businesses to streamline payment operations and improve customer experience, while intensifying competition with domestic payment processors. Merchants can now access Stripe’s global infrastructure for both e-commerce and brick-and-mortar sales.

perspective: Visa and Stripe expand in Asia as digital asset regulation and blockchain stability reshape the global payments landscape.
